title: Number lines: extra support (counting in tenths)

questions.q: A number line goes from 2 to 3 and is cut into 10 equal jumps. What is each jump worth?
questions.why: Between two whole numbers we have 10 equal jumps, so each is 1 tenth, or 0.1.
After 2.9 comes the next whole number. 9 tenths + 1 tenth = 10 tenths = 1 whole, so 2.9 + 0.1 = 3.0 (3). It is not 2.10.
3.9 + 0.1 = 4.0, which we write as 4. Then 4.1 comes next.

questions.q: Khalid counted in tenths and wrote 2.8, 2.9, 2.10, 2.11. What is his mistake?
questions.why: After 9 tenths you have a whole. 2.10 is not a tenths number. The line goes 2.9, 3.0, 3.1.

questions.q: A line goes 4, 4.2, 4.4, ___. What number comes next?
A line starts at 3 and jumps by 0.3: 3, 3.3, 3.6, ___
Keep jumping by 0.3 from 3.9. What is the next number?
Sophie starts at 3 and jumps 3 tenths each time. She says she will say 4.1. Is she correct?
questions.why: Her numbers go 3.3, 3.6, 3.9, 4.2. She skips right over 4.1, so she will not say it.

questions.q: A piece of wood sits on a 1 meter line cut into tenths. It starts at the 0.1 tick and ends at the 0.7 tick. How long is it, in meters?
questions.why: The wood does not start at 0, so do not just read the end tick. Count the jumps from 0.1 to 0.7: that is 6 tenths = 0.6 m.
